title: Customer churn prediction in telecom using machine learning in big data platform
harvard_reference: Ahmad, A.K., Jafar, A. and Aljoumaa, K. (2019) 'Customer churn prediction in telecom using machine learning in big data platform', Journal of Big Data, 6(1), article number 28. doi:10.1186/s40537-019-0191-6.
abstract_summary: The authors build a churn-prediction model for the Syrian mobile operator SyriaTel on a Hadoop/Spark big-data platform. Nine months of raw data (about 10 million customers, more than 70 TB, roughly 10,000 raw columns; churners about 5% of records) from five sources - customer/CRM data (subscription type, birthday, gender, location), towers and complaints databases, network logs, call detail records (charging information for calls, SMS, MMS and internet) and IMEI device data - are aggregated per customer into 'statistical' features (usage, complaints, device, competitor-contact percentages, coverage, etc.). A customer social graph is then built from four months of CDRs and Social Network Analysis (SNA) features (PageRank, Sender Rank, degree centrality, neighbour connectivity) are added. Four tree-based learners are compared using AUC: Decision Tree, Random Forest, GBM and XGBoost. With statistical features only the best AUC is 84%; adding SNA features raises XGBoost to 93.3% (GBM 90.89%, RF 87.76%, DT 83%). On a later, untouched 'NotOffered' population of 7.5 million prepaid customers XGBoost scores 89% AUC. The paper's stated contributions are the feature-engineering/selection pipeline on a big-data platform and the use of SNA features.

claims_supported.claim: Using rich behavioural data (call detail records, usage, complaints, network data) from SyriaTel, XGBoost reached an AUC of about 93 %, showing that richer behavioural features can lift performance well above what demographic and billing attributes alone achieve.
claims_supported.where: PARTLY supported, but the causal contrast in the second half is not made by the paper, so the claim as worded is not supported. (a) Supported: 'Data set' section lists customer/CRM data, towers and complaints database, network logs, CDRs and IMEI data; 'Data volume' subsection says data related to calls, SMS, MMS and internet 'with all related information like complaints, network data, IMEI, charging' were used; Abstract, Table 2 and Conclusion report XGBoost AUC 93.3% (93.301%). (b) NOT supported: the paper never trains or reports a model built only on demographic and/or billing attributes, so it cannot show that behavioural features beat such a baseline. Its only ablation (Table 2, 'Comparing AUC results before and after adding SNA to statistical features') is statistical features alone (XGBoost 84%, GBM 82%, RF 79.1%, DT 76%) versus statistical + SNA features (93.3%, 90.89%, 87.76%, 83%); the 84->93.3 gain is attributed specifically to Social Network Analysis features, not to behavioural versus demographic/billing data. Moreover the feature set already includes demographic fields (birthday, gender, location) and charging/billing data, so the comparison the claim implies is not one the study makes. Suggested rewording the source does support: 'Using nine months of CDR, usage, complaint, network-log and device data from SyriaTel, Ahmad et al. (2019) obtained an AUC of 93.3% with XGBoost; adding social-network-analysis features derived from the call graph raised AUC from 84% to 93.3%, illustrating how richer engineered features can substantially improve churn prediction.' Any contrast with demographic/billing-only datasets (e.g. the Kaggle Telco data) must be presented as the report author's own inference, not as a finding of this paper.

claims_supported.claim: [Verifier-proposed replacement] Using nine months of CDR, usage, complaint, network-log and device data from SyriaTel, XGBoost reached an AUC of 93.3%, and adding social-network-analysis features lifted AUC from 84% to 93.3%, showing that richer engineered features can substantially improve churn prediction.
claims_supported.where: Abstract ('the AUC value obtained is 93.3%'; 'The use of SNA enhanced the performance of the model from 84 to 93.3% against AUC standard'); 'Data set' section (five data sources incl. CDRs, complaints, network logs, IMEI); 'Data volume' subsection (nine months of transactions); Table 2 (statistical features 84% vs statistical + SNA 93.3% for XGBoost); Conclusion (XGBoost best, AUC 93.301%).

verification_notes: DOI 10.1186/s40537-019-0191-6 confirmed via CrossRef (journal-article, Journal of Big Data, vol 6, issue 1, article 28, 2019, Springer Science and Business Media LLC). Semantic Scholar (CorpusId 84186099, DBLP journals/jbd/AhmadJA19) and OpenAlex (published 2019-03-20, gold open access, 424 citations at time of check) agree on authors, title, venue and year. Verbatim abstract obtained from the arXiv export API for the preprint arXiv:1904.00690 (submitted 1 April 2019, journal-ref 'Journal of Big Data 2019 6:28'); NOTE the preprint title is longer ('...using machine learning and social network analysis in big data platform') - the published, CrossRef-registered title (used in the reference above) omits 'and social network analysis'. Springer landing page and PDF could not be fetched directly (cookie-authorisation redirect), so full-text checks were made on the arXiv PDF, which is the publisher's typeset version (24 pages, running header 'Ahmad et al. J Big Data (2019) 6:28'). Key full-text facts: ~10 million customers over nine months, >70 TB raw data, ~10,000 raw columns, churn class ~5%; prepaid customers; SNA graph built from last four months of CDRs; XGBoost 93.3% AUC (Table 2/3), GBM 90.89%, RF 87.76%, DT 83%; statistical-features-only best 84%; holdout on new 'NotOffered' data XGBoost 89% (Table 4). The lead's citation details ('Journal of Big Data 6, 28') were accurate. No page range exists; the article number is 28.
caveats: 1) The study does not contain a demographic/billing-only baseline; do not cite it as evidence that behavioural features beat demographic/billing attributes - cite it for the 93.3% AUC and for the 84->93.3% gain from SNA features. 2) The dataset is proprietary SyriaTel prepaid data, so results are not directly comparable to the public Kaggle/IBM Telco Customer Churn dataset (different customers, features, class balance ~5% vs ~27%, and no billing-contract variables of the same kind). 3) AUC values come from a single train/test split with no confidence intervals; performance on a later, untouched period fell to 89%. 4) Cite the published title, not the longer arXiv preprint title.
